cands.name: Jordan Lopez
cands.bio: Democrat representing North Carolina House District 112 (East Charlotte) since January 2025. A policy analyst, he previously worked in Gov. Roy Cooper's office and for state Sen. Mujtaba Mohammed. He holds a UNC Greensboro bachelor's degree and an NC Central University master's in public administration.

endorsements.text: Ballotpedia lists 2026 voter-guide recommendations from several Sway voting groups: Better Future NC, Beyond The Ballot, NC Public School Champions, Reject AIPAC from City Council to Congress, and Waves of Democracy.

cands.gaps: We found no documented actions in office (such as sponsored bills) tied to data centers, homestead property taxes, growth and land protection, immigration or H-1B, guns, or abortion. Ballotpedia's sponsored-legislation table was empty on the page we read. We found no stated positions from him on data centers, homestead taxes, guns, abortion or immigration. His campaign site supports more housing types and incremental development, but the page is undated, so we did not record it as a dated stance on development. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey in 2024 or 2026. We found no controversies, foreign ties or notable organizational endorsements.

local.label: Roots 100: His campaign site says he was born and raised in East Charlotte and attended Charlotte-Mecklenburg Schools, and Ballotpedia lists his birthplace as Charlotte, NC.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Sitting NC House member since January 2025 (first term). Earlier worked as a policy analyst in Gov. Roy Cooper's office and for state Sen. Mujtaba Mohammed in the NC Senate. Holds a master's in public administration.
qual.why: He has held a legislative seat and has a policy-staff career in the governor's office and the state Senate, which fits writing law and the budget. His legislative service is only one term, so the score is at the low end of the high range.

land-for-floridians.evidence: His campaign site says he supports putting an end to corporate homeownership concentrated in Mecklenburg County neighborhoods, so that new homes go to residents looking to own.

back-police-order.evidence: His campaign site says that ensuring Charlotte-Mecklenburg law enforcement has the resources to effectively prosecute and punish crime is vital. It also says he supports court staffing, community alternative-to-violence programs and mental health access.
